speaker: CROWLEY
text: Good evening from Hofstra University in Hempstead, New York.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: I’m Candy Crowley from CNN’s “State of the Union.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: ” We are here for the second presidential debate, a town hall, sponsored by the Commission on Presidential Debates.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: The Gallup organization chose 82 uncommitted voters from the New York area.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Their questions will drive the night.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: My goal is to give the conversation direction and to ensure questions get answered.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: The questions are known to me and my team only.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Neither the commission, nor the candidates have seen them.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: I hope to get to as many questions as possible.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: And because I am the optimistic sort, I’m sure the candidates will oblige by keeping their answers concise and on point.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Each candidate has as much as two minutes to respond to a common question, and there will be a two-minute follow-up.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: The audience here in the hall has agreed to be polite and attentive — no cheering or booing or outbursts of any sort.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: We will set aside that agreement just this once to welcome President Barack Obama and Governor Mitt Romney.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Gentlemen, thank you both for joining us here tonight.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: We have a lot of folks who’ve been waiting all day to talk to you, so I want to get right to it.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Governor Romney, as you know, you won the coin toss, so the first question will go to you.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: And I want to turn to a first-time voter, Jeremy Epstein, who has a question for you.

speaker: QUESTION
text: Mr.

speaker: QUESTION
text: President, Governor Romney, as a 20-year-old college student, all I hear from professors, neighbors and others is that when I graduate, I will have little chance to get employment.

speaker: QUESTION
text: What can you say to reassure me, but more importantly my parents, that I will be able to sufficiently support myself after I graduate?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Thank you, Jeremy.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I appreciate your — your question, and thank you for being here this evening and to all of those from Nassau County that have come, thank you for your time.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Thank you to Hofstra University and to Candy Crowley for organizing and leading this — this event.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Thank you, Mr.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: President, also for being part of this — this debate.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Your question — your question is one that’s being asked by college kids all over this country.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I was in Pennsylvania with someone who had just graduated — this was in Philadelphia — and she said, “I’ve got my degree.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I can’t find a job.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I’ve got three part- time jobs.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: They’re just barely enough to pay for my food and pay for an apartment.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I can’t begin to pay back my student loans.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: ” So what we have to do is two things.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We have to make sure that we make it easier for kids to afford college.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And also make sure that when they get out of college, there’s a job.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: When I was governor of Massachusetts, to get a high school degree, you had to pass an exam.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: If you graduated in the top quarter of your airlines, we gave you a John and Abigail Adams scholarship, four years tuition free in the college of your choice in Massachusetts, it’s a public institution.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I want to make sure we keep our Pell grant program growing.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We’re also going to have our loan program, so that people are able to afford school.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: But the key thing is to make sure you can get a job when you get out of school.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And what’s happened over the last four years has been very, very hard for America’s young people.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I want you to be able to get a job.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I know what it takes to get this economy going.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: With half of college kids graduating this year without a college — excuse me, without a job.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And without a college level job, that’s just unacceptable.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And likewise you’ve got more and more debt on your back.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: So more debt and less jobs.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I’m going to change that.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I know what it takes to create good jobs again.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I know what it takes to make sure that you have the kind of opportunity you deserve.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And kids across this country are going to recognize, we’re bringing back an economy.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: It’s not going to be like the last four years.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: The middle-class has been crushed over the last four years, and jobs have been too scarce.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I know what it takes to bring them back, and I’m going to do that, and make sure that when you graduate — when do you graduate?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: When you come out in 2014, I presume I’m going to be president.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I’m going to make sure you get a job.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Thanks Jeremy.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Yeah, you bet.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Mr.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: President?

speaker: OBAMA
text: Jeremy, first of all, your future is bright.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And the fact that you’re making an investment in higher education is critical.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Not just to you, but to the entire nation.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now, the most important thing we can do is to make sure that we are creating jobs in this country.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But not just jobs, good paying jobs.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Ones that can support a family.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And what I want to do, is build on the five million jobs that we’ve created over the last 30 months in the private sector alone.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And there are a bunch of things we can do to make sure your future is bright.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Number one, I want to build manufacturing jobs in this country again.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now when Governor Romney said we should let Detroit go bankrupt.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I said we’re going to bet on American workers and the American auto industry and it’s come surging back.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I want to do that in industries, not just in Detroit, but all across the country and that means we change our tax code so we’re giving incentives to companies that are investing here in the United States and creating jobs here.

speaker: OBAMA
text: It also means we’re helping them and small businesses to export all around the world to new markets.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Number two, we’ve got to make sure that we have the best education system in the world.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And the fact that you’re going to college is great, but I want everybody to get a great education and we’ve worked hard to make sure that student loans are available for folks like you, but I also want to make sure that community colleges are offering slots for workers to get retrained for the jobs that are out there right now and the jobs of the future.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Number three, we’ve got to control our own energy.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now, not only oil and natural gas, which we’ve been investing in; but also, we’ve got to make sure we’re building the energy source of the future, not just thinking about next year, but ten years from now, 20 years from now.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s why we’ve invested in solar and wind and biofuels, energy efficient cars.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We’ve got to reduce our deficit, but we’ve got to do it in a balanced way.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Asking the wealthy to pay a little bit more along with cuts so that we can invest in education like yours.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And let’s take the money that we’ve been spending on war over the last decade to rebuild America, roads, bridges schools.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We do those things, not only is your future going to be bright but America’s future is going to bright as well.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Let me ask you for more immediate answer and begin with Mr.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Romney just quickly what — what can you do?

speaker: CROWLEY
text: We’re looking at a situation where 40 percent of the unemployed have been unemployed have been unemployed for six months or more.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: They don’t have the two years that Jeremy has.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: What about those long term unemployed who need a job right now?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Well what you’re seeing in this country is 23 million people struggling to find a job.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And a lot of them, as you say, Candy, have been out of work for a long, long, long time.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: The president’s policies have been exercised over the last four years and they haven’t put Americans back to work.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We have fewer people working today than we had when the president took office.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: If the — the unemployment rate was 7.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: 8 percent when he took office, it’s 7.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: 8 percent now.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: But if you calculated that unemployment rate, taking back the people who dropped out of the workforce, it would be 10.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: 7 percent.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We have not made the progress we need to make to put people back to work.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: That’s why I put out a five-point plan that gets America 12 million new jobs in four years and rising take-home pay.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: It’s going to help Jeremy get a job when he comes out of school.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: It’s going to help people across the country that are unemployed right now.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And one thing that the president said, which I want to make sure that we understand, he said that I said we should take Detroit bankrupt.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And that’s right.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: My plan was to have the company go through bankruptcy like 7-Eleven did and Macy’s and Condell Airlines and come out stronger.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And I know he keeps saying, you want to take Detroit bankrupt.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Well, the president took Detroit bankrupt.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: You took General Motors bankrupt.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: You took Chrysler bankrupt.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: So when you say that I wanted to take the auto industry bankrupt, you actually did.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And I think it’s important to know that that was a process that was necessary to get those companies back on their feet, so they could start hiring more people.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: That was precisely what I recommended and ultimately what happened.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Let me give the president a chance.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Go ahead.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: OBAMA: Candy, what Governor Romney said just isn’t true.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: He wanted to take them into bankruptcy without providing them any way to stay open.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: And we would have lost a million jobs.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: And that — don’t take my word for it, take the executives at GM and Chrysler, some of whom are Republicans, may even support Governor Romney.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: But they’ll tell you his prescription wasn’t going to work.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: And Governor Romney’s says he’s got a five-point plan?

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Governor Romney doesn’t have a five-point plan.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: He has a one-point plan.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: And that plan is to make sure that folks at the top play by a different set of rules.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: That’s been his philosophy in the private sector, that’s been his philosophy as governor, that’s been his philosophy as a presidential candidate.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: You can make a lot of money and pay lower tax rates than somebody who makes a lot less.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: You can ship jobs overseas and get tax breaks for it.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: You can invest in a company, bankrupt it, lay off the workers, strip away their pensions, and you still make money.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: That’s exactly the philosophy that we’ve seen in place for the last decade.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: That’s what’s been squeezing middle class families.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: And we have fought back for four years to get out of that mess.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: The last thing we need to do is to go back to the very same policies that got us there.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Mr.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: President, the next question is going to be for you here.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: And, Mr.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Romney — Governor Romney — there’ll be plenty of chances here to go on, but I want to…

speaker: ROMNEY
text: That — that Detroit — that Detroit answer…

speaker: CROWLEY
text: We have all these folks.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: … that Detroit answer…

speaker: CROWLEY
text: I will let you absolutely…

speaker: ROMNEY
text: … and the rest of the answer, way off the mark.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: OK.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Will — will — you certainly will have lots of time here coming up.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Because I want to move you on to something that’s sort of connected to cars here, and — and go over.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: And we want to get a question from Phillip Tricolla.

speaker: QUESTION
text: Your energy secretary, Steven Chu, has now been on record three times stating it’s not policy of his department to help lower gas prices.

speaker: QUESTION
text: Do you agree with Secretary Chu that this is not the job of the Energy Department?

speaker: OBAMA
text: The most important thing we can do is to make sure we control our own energy.

speaker: OBAMA
text: So here’s what I’ve done since I’ve been president.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We have increased oil production to the highest levels in 16 years.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Natural gas production is the highest it’s been in decades.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We have seen increases in coal production and coal employment.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But what I’ve also said is we can’t just produce traditional source of energy.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We’ve also got to look to the future.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s why we doubled fuel efficiency standards on cars.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That means that in the middle of the next decade, any car you buy, you’re going to end up going twice as far on a gallon of gas.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s why we doubled clean — clean energy production like wind and solar and biofuels.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And all these things have contributed to us lowering our oil imports to the lowest levels in 16 years.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now, I want to build on that.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And that means, yes, we still continue to open up new areas for drilling.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We continue to make it a priority for us to go after natural gas.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We’ve got potentially 600,000 jobs and 100 years worth of energy right beneath our feet with natural gas.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And we can do it in an environmentally sound way.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But we’ve also got to continue to figure out how we have efficiency energy, because ultimately that’s how we’re going to reduce demand and that’s what’s going to keep gas prices lower.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now, Governor Romney will say he’s got an all-of-the-above plan, but basically his plan is to let the oil companies write the energy policies.

speaker: OBAMA
text: So he’s got the oil and gas part, but he doesn’t have the clean energy part.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And if we are only thinking about tomorrow or the next day and not thinking about 10 years from now, we’re not going to control our own economic future.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Because China, Germany, they’re making these investments.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And I’m not going to cede those jobs of the future to those countries.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I expect those new energy sources to be built right here in the United States.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s going to help Jeremy get a job.

speaker: OBAMA
text: It’s also going to make sure that you’re not paying as much for gas.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Governor, on the subject of gas prices?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Well, let’s look at the president’s policies, all right, as opposed to the rhetoric, because we’ve had four years of policies being played out.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And the president’s right in terms of the additional oil production, but none of it came on federal land.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: As a matter of fact, oil production is down 14 percent this year on federal land, and gas production was down 9 percent.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Why?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Because the president cut in half the number of licenses and permits for drilling on federal lands, and in federal waters.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: So where’d the increase come from?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Well a lot of it came from the Bakken Range in North Dakota.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: What was his participation there?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: The administration brought a criminal action against the people drilling up there for oil, this massive new resource we have.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And what was the cost?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: 20 or 25 birds were killed and brought out a migratory bird act to go after them on a criminal basis.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Look, I want to make sure we use our oil, our coal, our gas, our nuclear, our renewables.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I believe very much in our renewable capabilities; ethanol, wind, solar will be an important part of our energy mix.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: But what we don’t need is to have the president keeping us from taking advantage of oil, coal and gas.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: This has not been Mr.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Oil, or Mr.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Gas, or Mr.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Coal.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Talk to the people that are working in those industries.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I was in coal country.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: People grabbed my arms and said, “Please save my job.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: ” The head of the EPA said, “You can’t build a coal plant.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: You’ll virtually — it’s virtually impossible given our regulations.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: ” When the president ran for office, he said if you build a coal plant, you can go ahead, but you’ll go bankrupt.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: That’s not the right course for America.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Let’s take advantage of the energy resources we have, as well as the energy sources for the future.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And if we do that, if we do what I’m planning on doing, which is getting us energy independent, North America energy independence within eight years, you’re going to see manufacturing jobs come back.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Because our energy is low cost, that are already beginning to come back because of our abundant energy.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I’ll get America and North America energy independent.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I’ll do it by more drilling, more permits and licenses.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We’re going to bring that pipeline in from Canada.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: How in the world the president said no to that pipeline?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I will never know.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: This is about bringing good jobs back for the middle class of America, and that’s what I’m going to do.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: CROWLEY: Mr.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: President, let me just see if I can move you to the gist of this question, which is, are we looking at the new normal?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I can tell you that tomorrow morning, a lot of people in Hempstead will wake up and fill up and they will find that the price of gas is over $4 a gallon.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Is it within the purview of the government to bring those prices down, or are we looking at the new normal?

speaker: OBAMA
text: Candy, there’s no doubt that world demand’s gone up, but our production is going up, and we’re using oil more efficiently.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And very little of what Governor Romney just said is true.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We’ve opened up public lands.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We’re actually drilling more on public lands than in the previous administration and my — the previous president was an oil man.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And natural gas isn’t just appearing magically.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We’re encouraging it and working with the industry.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And when I hear Governor Romney say he’s a big coal guy, I mean, keep in mind, when — Governor, when you were governor of Massachusetts, you stood in front of a coal plant and pointed at it and said, “This plant kills,” and took great pride in shutting it down.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And now suddenly you’re a big champion of coal.

speaker: OBAMA
text: So what I’ve tried to do is be consistent.

speaker: OBAMA
text: With respect to something like coal, we made the largest investment in clean coal technology, to make sure that even as we’re producing more coal, we’re producing it cleaner and smarter.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Same thing with oil, same thing with natural gas.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And the proof is our oil imports are down to the lowest levels in 20 years.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Oil production is up, natural gas production is up, and, most importantly, we’re also starting to build cars that are more efficient.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And that’s creating jobs.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That means those cars can be exported, ’cause that’s the demand around the world, and it also means that it’ll save money in your pocketbook.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s the strategy you need, an all-of-the-above strategy, and that’s what we’re going to do in the next four years.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: But that’s not what you’ve done in the last four years.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: That’s the problem.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: In the last four years, you cut permits and licenses on federal land and federal waters in half.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Not true, Governor Romney.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: So how much did you cut ?

speaker: OBAMA
text: Not true.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: How much did you cut them by, then?

speaker: OBAMA
text: Governor, we have actually produced more oil —

speaker: ROMNEY
text: No, no.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: How much did you cut licenses and permits on federal land and federal waters?

speaker: OBAMA
text: Governor Romney, here’s what we did.

speaker: OBAMA
text: There were a whole bunch of oil companies.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: No, no, I had a question and the question was how much did you cut them by?

speaker: OBAMA
text: You want me to answer a question —

speaker: ROMNEY
text: How much did you cut them by?

speaker: OBAMA
text: I’m happy to answer the question.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: All right.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And it is —

speaker: OBAMA
text: Here’s what happened.

speaker: OBAMA
text: You had a whole bunch of oil companies who had leases on public lands that they weren’t using.

speaker: OBAMA
text: So what we said was you can’t just sit on this for 10, 20, 30 years, decide when you want to drill, when you want to produce, when it’s most profitable for you.

speaker: OBAMA
text: These are public lands.

speaker: OBAMA
text: So if you want to drill on public lands, you use it or you lose it.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: OK, —

speaker: OBAMA
text: And so what we did was take away those leases.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And we are now reletting them so that we can actually make a profit.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And production on private — on government land —

speaker: OBAMA
text: Production is up.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: — is down.

speaker: OBAMA
text: No, it isn’t.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Production on government land of oil is down 14 percent.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Governor —

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And production on gas —

speaker: OBAMA
text: It’s just not true.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: It’s absolutely true.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Look, there’s no question but the people recognize that we have not produced more on federal lands and in federal waters.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And coal, coal production is not up; coal jobs are not up.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I was just at a coal facility, where some 1,200 people lost their jobs.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: The right course for America is to have a true all-of-the-above policy.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I don’t think anyone really believes that you’re a person who’s going to be pushing for oil and gas and coal.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: You’ll get your chance in a moment.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I’m still speaking.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Well —

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And the answer is I don’t believe people think that’s the case —

speaker: ROMNEY
text: That wasn’t the question.

speaker: OBAMA
text: OK.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: That was a statement.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I don’t think the American people believe that.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I will fight for oil, coal and natural gas.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And the proof, the proof of whether a strategy is working or not is what the price is that you’re paying at the pump.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: If you’re paying less than you paid a year or two ago, why, then, the strategy is working.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: But you’re paying more.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: When the president took office, the price of gasoline here in Nassau County was about $1.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: 86 a gallon.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Now, it’s $4.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: 00 a gallon.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: The price of electricity is up.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: If the president’s energy policies are working, you’re going to see the cost of energy come down.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I will fight to create more energy in this country, to get America energy secure.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And part of that is bringing in a pipeline of oil from Canada, taking advantage of the oil and coal we have here, drilling offshore in Alaska, drilling offshore in Virginia where the people want it.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Those things will get us the energy we need.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Mr.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: President, could you address, because we did finally get to gas prices here, could you address what the governor said, which is if your energy policy was working, the price of gasoline would not be $4 a gallon here.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Is that true?

speaker: OBAMA
text: Well, think about what the governor — think about what the governor just said.

speaker: OBAMA
text: He said when I took office, the price of gasoline was $1.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Why is that?

speaker: OBAMA
text: Because the economy was on the verge of collapse, because we were about to go through the worst recession since the Great Depression, as a consequence of some of the same policies that Governor Romney’s now promoting.

speaker: OBAMA
text: So, it’s conceivable that Governor Romney could bring down gas prices because with his policies, we might be back in that same mess.

speaker: OBAMA
text: What I want to do is to create an economy that is strong, and at the same time produce energy.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And with respect to this pipeline that Governor Romney keeps on talking about, we’ve — we’ve built enough pipeline to wrap around the entire earth once.

speaker: OBAMA
text: So, I’m all for pipelines.

speaker: OBAMA

text: And she worked hard every day and made a lot of sacrifices to make sure we got everything we needed.

text: My grandmother, she started off as a secretary in a bank.

text: Making sure that we are controlling our own energy, but not only the energy of today, but also the energy of the future.

text: We welcome people coming to this country as immigrants.

text: My dad was born in Mexico of American parents; Ann’s dad was born in Wales and is a first-generation American.

text: We welcome legal immigrants into this country.

text: I want our legal system to work better.

text: I want it to be streamlined.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I want it to be clearer.

text: I don’t think you have to — shouldn’t have to hire a lawyer to figure out how to get into this country legally.

text: I also think that we should give visas to people — green cards, rather, to people who graduate with skills that we need.

text: People around the world with accredited degrees in science and math get a green card stapled to their diploma, come to the U.

text: of A.

text: We should make sure our legal system works.

text: Number two, we’re going to have to stop illegal immigration.

text: There are 4 million people who are waiting in line to get here legally.

text: Those who’ve come here illegally take their place.

text: So I will not grant amnesty to those who have come here illegally.

text: What I will do is I’ll put in place an employment verification system and make sure that employers that hire people who have come here illegally are sanctioned for doing so.

text: The kids of those that came here illegally, those kids, I think, should have a pathway to become a permanent resident of the United States and military service, for instance, is one way they would have that kind of pathway to become a permanent resident.

text: Now when the president ran for office, he said that he’d put in place, in his first year, a piece of legislation — he’d file a bill in his first year that would reform our — our immigration system, protect legal immigration, stop illegal immigration.

text: The first thing we did was to streamline the legal immigration system, to reduce the backlog, make it easier, simpler and cheaper for people who are waiting in line, obeying the law to make sure that they can come here and contribute to our country and that’s good for our economic growth.

text: They’ll make things happen to create jobs here in the United States.

text: Number two, we do have to deal with our border so we put more border patrol on the — any time in history and the flow of undocumented works across the border is actually lower than it’s been in 40 years.

text: What I’ve also said is if we’re going to go after folks who are here illegally, we should do it smartly and go after folks who are criminals, gang bangers, people who are hurting the community, not after students, not after folks who are here just because they’re trying to figure out how to feed their families.

text: And what I’ve also said is for young people who come here, brought here often times by their parents.

text: Had gone to school here, pledged allegiance to the flag.

text: Think of this as their country.

text: Understand themselves as Americans in every way except having papers.

text: And we should make sure that we give them a pathway to citizenship.

text: ” His main strategy during the Republican primary was to say, “We’re going to encourage self-deportation.

text: It’s not by trickle-down government, saying we’re going to take more money from people and hire more government workers, raise more taxes, put in place more regulations.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Trickle-down government has never worked here, has never worked anywhere.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I want to make America the most attractive place in the world for entrepreneurs, for small business, for big business, to invest and grow in America.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Now, we’re going to have to make sure that as we trade with other nations that they play by the rules.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And China hasn’t.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: One of the reasons — or one of the ways they don’t play by the rules is artificially holding down the value of their currency.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Because if they put their currency down low, that means their prices on their goods are low.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And that makes them advantageous in the marketplace.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We lose sales.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And manufacturers here in the U.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: making the same products can’t compete.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: China has been a currency manipulator for years and years and years.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And the president has a regular opportunity to label them as a currency manipulator, but refuses to do so.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: On day one, I will label China a currency manipulator, which will allow me as president to be able to put in place, if necessary, tariffs where I believe that they are taking unfair advantage of our manufacturers.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: So we’re going to make sure that people we trade with around the world play by the rules.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: But let me — let me not just stop there.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Don’t forget, what’s key to bringing back jobs here is not just finding someone else to punish, and I’m going to be strict with people who we trade with to make sure they — they follow the law and play by the rules, but it’s also to make America the most attractive place in the world for businesses of all kinds.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: That’s why I want to down the tax rates on small employers, big employers, so they want to be here.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Canada’s tax rate on companies is now 15 percent.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Ours is 35 percent.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: So if you’re starting a business, where would you rather start it?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We have to be competitive if we’re going to create more jobs here.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Regulations have quadrupled.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: The rate of regulations quadrupled under this president.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I talk to small businesses across the country.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: They say, “We feel like we’re under attack from our own government.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: ” I want to make sure that regulators see their job as encouraging small business, not crushing it.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And there’s no question but that Obamacare has been an extraordinary deterrent to enterprises of all kinds hiring people.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: My priority is making sure that we get more people hired.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: If we have more people hired, if we get back manufacturing jobs, if we get back all kinds of jobs into this country, then you’re going to see rising incomes again.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: The reason incomes are down is because unemployment is so high.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I know what it takes to get this to happen, and my plan will do that, and one part of it is to make sure that we keep China playing by the rules.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Mr.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: President, two minutes here, because we are then going to go to our last question.

speaker: OBAMA
text: OK.

speaker: OBAMA
text: We need to create jobs here.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And both Governor Romney and I agree actually that we should lower our corporate tax rate.

speaker: OBAMA
text: It’s too high.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But there’s a difference in terms of how we would do it.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I want to close loopholes that allow companies to deduct expenses when they move to China; that allow them to profit offshore and not have to get taxed, so they have tax advantages offshore.

speaker: OBAMA
text: All those changes in our tax code would make a difference.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now, Governor Romney actually wants to expand those tax breaks.

speaker: OBAMA
text: One of his big ideas when it comes to corporate tax reform would be to say, if you invest overseas, you make profits overseas, you don’t have to pay U.

speaker: OBAMA
text: taxes.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But, of course, if you’re a small business or a mom-and-pop business or a big business starting up here, you’ve got to pay even the reduced rate that Governor Romney’s talking about.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And it’s estimated that that will create 800,000 new jobs.

speaker: OBAMA
text: The problem is they’ll be in china.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Or India.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Or Germany.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s not the way we’re going to create jobs here.

speaker: OBAMA
text: The way we’re going to create jobs here is not just to change our tax code, but also to double our exports.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And we are on pace to double our exports, one of the commitments I made when I was president.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s creating tens of thousands of jobs all across the country.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s why we’ve kept on pushing trade deals, but trade deals that make sure that American workers and American businesses are getting a good deal.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Now, Governor Romney talked about China, as I already indicated.

speaker: OBAMA
text: In the private sector, Governor Romney’s company invested in what were called pioneers of outsourcing.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s not my phrase.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s what reporters called it.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And as far as currency manipulation, the currency has actually gone up 11 percent since I’ve been president because we have pushed them hard.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And we’ve put unprecedented trade pressure on China.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s why exports have significantly increased under my presidency.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s going to help to create jobs here.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Mr.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: President, we have a really short time for a quick discussion here.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: iPad, the Macs, the iPhones, they are all manufactured in China.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: One of the major reasons is labor is so much cheaper here.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: How do you convince a great American company to bring that manufacturing back here?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: The answer is very straightforward.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We can compete with anyone in the world as long as the playing field is level.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: China’s been cheating over the years.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: One by holding down the value of their currency.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Number two, by stealing our intellectual property; our designs, our patents, our technology.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: There’s even an Apple store in China that’s a counterfeit Apple store, selling counterfeit goods.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: They hack into our computers.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We will have to have people play on a fair basis, that’s number one.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Number two, we have to make America the most attractive place for entrepreneurs, for people who want to expand their business.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: That’s what brings jobs in.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: The president’s characterization of my tax plan…

speaker: ROMNEY
text: …is completely…is completely…

speaker: ROMNEY
text: …is completely false.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Let me tell you…

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Let me to go the president here because we really are running out of time.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: And the question is can we ever get — we can’t get wages like that.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: It can’t be sustained.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Candy, there are some jobs that are not going to come back.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Because they are low wage, low skill jobs.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I want high wage, high skill jobs.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s why we have to emphasize manufacturing.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s why we have to invest in advanced manufacturing.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s why we’ve got to make sure that we’ve got the best science and research in the world.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And when we talk about deficits, if we’re adding to our deficit for tax cuts for folks who don’t need them, and we’re cutting investments in research and science that will create the next Apple, create the next new innovation that will sell products around the world, we will lose that race.

speaker: OBAMA
text: If we’re not training engineers to make sure that they are equipped here in this country.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Then companies won’t come here.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Those investments are what’s going to help to make sure that we continue to lead this world economy, not just next year, but 10 years from now, 50 years from now, 100 years from now.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Thanks Mr.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: President.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Governor Romney?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Government does not create jobs.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Government does not create jobs.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Governor Romney, I want to introduce you to Barry Green, because he’s going to have the last question to you first?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Barry?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Where is Barry?

speaker: QUESTION
text: Hi, Governor.

speaker: QUESTION
text: I think this is a tough question.

speaker: QUESTION
text: To each of you.

speaker: QUESTION
text: What do you believe is the biggest misperception that the American people have about you as a man and a candidate?

speaker: QUESTION
text: Using specific examples, can you take this opportunity to debunk that misperception and set us straight?

speaker: ROMNEY
text: Thank you, and that’s an opportunity for me, and I appreciate it.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: In the nature of a campaign, it seems that some campaigns are focused on attacking a person rather than prescribing their own future and the things they’d like to do.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: In the course of that, I think the president’s campaign has tried to characterize me as — as someone who’s very different than who I am.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I care about 100 percent of the American people.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I want 100 percent of the American people to have a bright and prosperous future.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I care about our kids.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I understand what it takes to make a bright and prosperous future for America again.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I spent my life in the private sector, not in government.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I’m a guy who wants to help with the experience I have, the American people.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: My — my passion probably flows from the fact that I believe in God.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And I believe we’re all children of the same God.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I believe we have a responsibility to care for one another.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I — I served as a missionary for my church.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I served as a pastor in my congregation for about 10 years.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I’ve sat across the table from people who were out of work and worked with them to try and find new work or to help them through tough times.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I went to the Olympics when they were in trouble to try and get them on track.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And as governor of my state, I was able to get 100 percent of my people insured, all my kids, about 98 percent of the adults.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I was able also to get our schools ranked number one in the nation, so 100 percent of our kids would have a bright opportunity for a future.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I understand that I can get this country on track again.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We don’t have to settle for what we’re going through.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We don’t have to settle for gasoline at four bucks.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We don’t have to settle for unemployment at a chronically high level.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We don’t have to settle for 47 million people on food stamps.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We don’t have to settle for 50 percent of kids coming out of college not able to get work.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: We don’t have to settle for 23 million people struggling to find a good job.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: If I become president, I’ll get America working again.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I will get us on track to a balanced budget.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: The president hasn’t.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I will.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I’ll make sure we can reform Medicare and Social Security to preserve them for coming — coming generations.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: The president said he would.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: He didn’t.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Governor…

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I’ll get our incomes up.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: And by the way, I’ve done these things.

speaker: ROMNEY
text: I served as governor and showed I could get them done.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Mr.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: President, last two minutes belong to you.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Barry, I think a lot of this campaign, maybe over the last four years, has been devoted to this nation that I think government creates jobs, that that somehow is the answer.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s not what I believe.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I believe that the free enterprise system is the greatest engine of prosperity the world’s ever known.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I believe in self-reliance and individual initiative and risk takers being rewarded.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But I also believe that everybody should have a fair shot and everybody should do their fair share and everybody should play by the same rules, because that’s how our economy’s grown.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s how we built the world’s greatest middle class.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And — and that is part of what’s at stake in this election.

speaker: OBAMA
text: There’s a fundamentally different vision about how we move our country forward.

speaker: OBAMA
text: I believe Governor Romney is a good man.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Loves his family, cares about his faith.

speaker: OBAMA
text: But I also believe that when he said behind closed doors that 47 percent of the country considered themselves victims who refuse personal responsibility, think about who he was talking about.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Folks on Social Security who’ve worked all their lives.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Veterans who’ve sacrificed for this country.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Students who are out there trying to hopefully advance their own dreams, but also this country’s dreams.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Soldiers who are overseas fighting for us right now.

speaker: OBAMA
text: People who are working hard every day, paying payroll tax, gas taxes, but don’t make enough income.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And I want to fight for them.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s what I’ve been doing for the last four years.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Because if they succeed, I believe the country succeeds.

speaker: OBAMA
text: When my grandfather fought in World War II and he came back and he got a G.

speaker: OBAMA
text: Bill and that allowed him to go to college, that wasn’t a handout.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That was something that advanced the entire country.

speaker: OBAMA
text: And I want to make sure that the next generation has those same opportunities.

speaker: OBAMA
text: That’s why I’m asking for your vote and that’s why I’m asking for another four years.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: President Obama, Governor Romney, thank you for being here tonight.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: On that note we have come to an end of this town hall debate.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Our thanks to the participants for their time and to the people of Hofstra University for their hospitality.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: The next and final debate takes place Monday night at Lynn University in Boca Raton, Florida.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Don’t forget to watch.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Election Day is three weeks from today.

speaker: CROWLEY
text: Don’t forget to vote.

text: Good night.
